# AMD Technical Report (as of 2026-10-21)

## 1. Bottom line

AMD is in a **sharp pullback inside a larger, intact uptrend**. The short-term trend has turned down and the long-term trend is still up.

- The close on 2026-10-21 was **552.72**. That is about 14.9% below the cycle-high close of **649.42** (2026-10-06) and about 4.5% above the pullback-low close of **528.75** (2026-10-16).
- Short-term momentum has rolled over: MACD is below zero and below its signal line, and price is under the 10 EMA, the 20-day Bollinger midline and the VWMA.
- The medium- and long-term structure is intact: price is above the rising 50 SMA (541.10) and far above the 200 SMA (399.08).
- The setup is a contest at the 50 SMA. A hold and a reclaim of the short-term averages would favor the uptrend resuming. A failure would shift attention to the lower Bollinger band and the 10/16 lows.

This report describes what the indicators show. It is not a trade instruction.

## 2. Data integrity

- Every indicator value from `get_indicators` that is also in the verified snapshot matches it: 10 EMA 566.04, 50 SMA 541.10, 200 SMA 399.08, RSI 45.07, Bollinger midline 598.98, MACD -2.17 and ATR 26.55. **No discrepancies were found.**
- **VWMA (589.91 on 10/21)** is not in the snapshot. It comes only from `get_indicators` and has no conflicting source.
- **MACD signal (11.12), MACD histogram (-13.29), Bollinger upper (674.69) and Bollinger lower (523.27)** come from the snapshot only. I did not pull them as separate time series, so I can't describe their recent paths.
- The 8 indicators I selected were: `close_50_sma`, `close_200_sma`, `close_10_ema`, `macd`, `rsi`, `boll`, `atr` and `vwma`.

## 3. Price context

- **Year-to-date run:** AMD closed at 284.49 on 2026-04-21 and 649.42 on 2026-10-06, more than doubling in about six months.
- **June 30 high:** The 2026-06-30 close was 580.91 and the intraday high was 584.73. The stock then fell to a 429.56 close on 2026-07-29.
- **August to mid-September range:** Closes ran from about 456 to 521, with low volume. Daily volume was often 12–19M, versus 30M or more in the spring.
- **September breakout:** The close on 2026-09-21 was 615.52, up from 559.82 on 9/18. Volume was 44.49M, the heaviest session in the recent window. That move cleared the 6/30 high area (580.91 close, 584.73 high).
- **October peak and drop:** After the 649.42 close on 10/6, the stock fell to 645.86 (10/7), 620.68 (10/8), 608.10 (10/9), 594.24 (10/12), a bounce to 605.53 (10/13), then 570.82 (10/14), 562.23 (10/15) and 528.75 (10/16).
- **Gap-down:** On 10/15 the stock opened at 540.00 after a 570.82 close the day before.
- **Round trip:** The selloff took price back below the 6/30 high area (580.91 close, 584.73 high). Price has since stabilized in the 530–555 range for the last three sessions.
- **Last three closes:** 538.05 (10/19), 534.74 (10/20) and 552.72 (10/21). The last was a +3.4% day. Its range was 537.30–556.79 on 17.87M shares.

## 4. Indicator analysis

### Trend: moving averages

| Indicator | 10/21 value | Price vs. level | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 EMA | 566.04 | Price below | Short-term trend is down |
| 50 SMA | 541.10 | Price above (~2.1%) | Medium-term trend is up, being tested |
| 200 SMA | 399.08 | Price above (~38.5%) | Long-term trend is strongly up |

- **10 EMA:** It peaked at 622.68 (10/7) and has fallen every session since, to 566.04. Price crossed below it on the 10/14 to 10/15 drop. It is now the first overhead resistance reference.
- **50 SMA:**
  - It is still rising, from 537.14 (10/16) to 541.10 (10/21).
  - Price closed below it on 10/16 (528.75 vs. 537.14), 10/19 (538.05 vs. 538.23, a razor-thin miss) and 10/20 (534.74 vs. 539.54).
  - The 10/21 close of 552.72 **reclaimed it**. That is a modestly constructive development, but it is one session old.
- **200 SMA:** It rose from 356.63 (9/21) to 399.08 (10/21). It is far from price, so it works as a strategic trend confirmation, not a near-term level.
- **Compression:** The 10 EMA minus 50 SMA gap was about 100 points on 10/7 (622.68 vs. 522.64). It is now about 25 points (566.04 vs. 541.10). If weakness continues, the 10 EMA could cross below the 50 SMA, a short-term bearish signal. A bounce would widen the gap again.

### Momentum: MACD

- The MACD line is **-2.17**, the signal line is **11.12** and the histogram is **-13.29**.
- The MACD line peaked at 36.55 (10/7). It crossed below zero on 10/20 (-0.59) and fell further on 10/21, even on an up day. That is a lagging effect of the prior decline.
- The line is below its signal line and the histogram is negative, so **momentum is bearish on this measure**. A bullish signal would need the MACD line to turn up and the histogram to narrow toward zero. Today's data show neither.
- The MACD has not yet confirmed the 10/21 bounce, so treat that bounce with caution.

### Momentum: RSI

- RSI is **45.07**, up from a window low of **37.77** (10/16) and 39.81 (10/20).
- It was above 70 on 10/2 (70.07), 10/6 (72.16) and 10/7 (70.71). It was also near 73 in the 9/21 to 9/25 period (72.99 on 9/25).
- **Mild bearish divergence:** Price made a higher closing high on 10/6 (649.42) than on 9/25 (630.63). RSI at 72.16 was slightly below its 9/25 level of 72.99. The divergence is small, but it fits the reversal that followed.
- At 45, RSI is neither oversold nor overbought. It did not reach 30 on this pullback, which is consistent with a correction in an uptrend, not a trend break. It is still below 50, so momentum has not recovered.

### Volatility: Bollinger Bands and ATR

- **Bands:** Middle 598.98, upper 674.69 and lower 523.27. Price at 552.72 sits in the lower half of the bands, between the lower band and the midline. The band width is about 151 points, which is wide.
- **Midline:** It peaked at 611.95 (10/15) and has fallen to 598.98. Price has stayed below it since 10/14.
- **Lower band:** At 523.27 it sits just under the 10/16 closing low (528.75) and the 10/20 intraday low (524.60). The 10/16 intraday low was 526.83. Because I don't have the lower band's history, I can't say when price last touched it.
- **ATR:** It is **26.55** (about 4.8% of price). It peaked at 27.27 on 10/16 and has eased since. Daily swings of 25–30 points are normal at this volatility.
- **Position sizing and stops (illustrative):**
  - 1.5× ATR ≈ 40 points.
  - 2× ATR ≈ 53 points.
  - Tight stops placed inside one ATR are likely to be hit by noise.
  - Size positions with the wide ATR in mind.

### Volume-weighted trend: VWMA

- VWMA is **589.91**, versus a close of 552.72. Price is below it.
- It peaked at 623.51 (10/9) and has declined each session since.
- Price below VWMA suggests much of the recent heavy-volume trading happened at higher prices. That is overhead supply and an obstacle to a quick recovery.
- **Volume pattern:**
  - The decline days had heavy volume: 22.32M on 10/14, 28.83M on 10/15 and 22.58M on 10/16.
  - The latest bounce volume is lighter: 17.87M on 10/21 and 15.19M on 10/20.
  - Volume is not yet confirming a recovery. A rebound on rising volume would be a stronger sign.

## 5. Reference levels

These are reference levels derived from the indicators and the price data. I have not claimed historical bounces or validation at any of them.

**Overhead (resistance candidates):**
- 556.79: the 10/21 high.
- 566.04: the 10 EMA.

- 589.91: the VWMA.

**Below (support candidates):**

- 526.83: the 10/16 intraday low.

- 399.08: the 200 SMA, a long way down.

## 6. Scenarios

**Constructive case (uptrend resumes):**
- Price holds above the 50 SMA (541.10) and closes back above the 10 EMA (566.04).
- Then it targets the 580–585 zone, the VWMA near 590 and the Bollinger midline near 599.
- Confirmation would be the MACD histogram narrowing, RSI back above 50, and volume rising on up days.
- Supports this case: the rising 50 and 200 SMAs, RSI never reaching oversold, and the 10/21 reclaim of the 50 SMA.

**Cautionary case (pullback deepens):**
- Price closes back below the 50 SMA and the 10/21 low (537.30).
- The next reference is the 10/16 low area (526.83 to 528.75) and the lower band (523.27).
- A close below that area would leave little nearby support in the data until the pre-breakout range (493 to 516).
- Supports this case: negative MACD with a negative histogram, price below the 10 EMA, VWMA and Bollinger midline, and heavier volume on the down days.

**Current lean:** The short-term evidence leans bearish to neutral. The longer-term evidence is bullish. The 10/21 bounce is unconfirmed by momentum or volume. The next few sessions around the 50 SMA and 10 EMA should be decisive.

# AMD: News, Macro and Sentiment Report (week to 2026-10-21)

## Data coverage
- **Available:** AMD and global news headlines (headline and source only, no article bodies), and Polymarket probabilities.
- **Unavailable:** All five FRED macro calls (fed funds, 10y Treasury, CPI, unemployment, VIX) failed because no FRED API key is configured. I give no rate, inflation, labor or volatility levels and have not estimated any. The macro view below rests only on prediction markets and headlines.
- **Not in the headlines:** The Susquehanna price target figures, AMD's exact earnings date, and any consensus estimates.

## 1. AMD-specific news
**Overall tone:** Bullish and crowded going into earnings. Several headlines say AMD is "priced for perfection."

- **Analyst support:** Susquehanna raised its AMD and Qualcomm targets and cut Intel and Coherent. It sees "modest upside" for chip earnings. The AMD target raise was framed as coming "ahead of earnings."
- **Price action:**
  - AMD gained 1.8% on one day on "AI ambition."
  - It was named among "soaring" semiconductor stocks with Teradyne, Vishay, Allegro and Entegris.
  - A 24/7 Wall St. piece cites a **137% run** and asks whether AMD is priced for perfection before earnings.
- **Demand signal:** Anthropic has reportedly locked in over **$600B of computing** and still wants more, which 24/7 Wall St. calls "big news for AMD." This supports the AI accelerator demand story, but the headline doesn't say AMD's share of that spend.
- **Fundamentals:** Insider Monkey says AMD's data center business is "finally delivering profits" and asks whether it can sustain the momentum. This is the key metric to watch in the print.
- **Competitive context:**
  - Several AMD-vs-Nvidia comparison pieces ran this week.
  - Intel rose after Musk signaled a "Terafab breakthrough," a possible longer-term foundry competitor and sentiment cross-current.
  - Supermicro raised its revenue forecast, which is a positive read-through for AI server demand.
  - Credo surged 6.25% on AI memory momentum.

## 2. Sector and market backdrop
- A WSJ headline says SpaceX, Anthropic and Nvidia helped tech "snap out of their recent malaise." That implies tech was weak before this week, so the rebound is recent.
- The semiconductor tape was broadly strong: MACOM, Semtech, FormFactor, Seagate, Western Digital, Monolithic Power and Texas Instruments all appeared in "shares up or skyrocket" lists.
- **Earnings season:** Meta, Tesla, IBM and TI beat Q3 estimates. IBM rose on software strength. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained, and the Dow popped on the Nasdaq's strength.
- **Other markets:** Gold edged higher as oil retreated. A falling oil price is mildly disinflationary, but I can't quantify it without data.

## 3. Macro signals from prediction markets
- **Fed:** Polymarket gives **97%** to no Fed rate cuts in 2026, with $9.0M volume and little change on the week. Markets with 6 to 12 cuts are priced at about 0%. With a cut off the table for 2026, AMD's high-multiple valuation can't count on lower discount rates.
- **Recession:** The probability of a US recession by end-2026 is **8%** ($2.3M volume). The UK and Japan are each about 4%, though those markets are thinly traded. The market sees low near-term macro tail risk.

## 4. Trading implications
1. **Event risk is the main driver.** The stock has run hard (+137%) into earnings, so the print has to meet elevated expectations. Watch data center and Instinct GPU revenue, margins, and the guide. Also watch whether commentary supports the large AI compute commitments, such as Anthropic's. A strong beat with a muted reaction is plausible. A guide-down could cause a sharp drawdown.
2. **Positioning:** Analyst target raises and a broad semiconductor rally suggest crowded long positioning. Consider smaller sizes, defined-risk options structures such as spreads, or hedges with peers. Implied volatility likely rises into the print, but I couldn't verify it.
3. **Macro:** A static Fed (no cuts priced) and a low recession probability favor continued AI-led risk appetite. A yield spike or hawkish surprise is the main macro risk to long-duration growth names. I couldn't check yields or the VIX.
4. **Read-throughs:** Nvidia, Supermicro, Credo and other AI hardware names' results and guides will move AMD. Intel/Terafab headlines are a sentiment wildcard.
5. **Levels to check:** Price levels, support and resistance, and the earnings date and consensus all need confirming from another source.

## Summary table

| AMD sentiment | Bullish, but flagged as "priced for perfection" | 24/7 Wall St.: 137% run into earnings | High bar for the print; asymmetric downside on a miss |
| Analysts | Susquehanna raised its AMD target (figure not given), cut Intel | GuruFocus, Stocktwits | Supportive, but a lagging, crowded signal |
| AI demand | Anthropic has locked in over $600B of compute and wants more | 24/7 Wall St. | Long-term tailwind; AMD's share is unspecified |
| Fundamentals | Data center is "finally delivering profits" | Insider Monkey | Margin and data center guide are the key items on the print |
| Sector | Semis broadly strong; Supermicro raised its forecast; Credo +6.25% | StockStory, Yahoo Finance | Positive read-through, but beta-driven |
| Competition | Intel up on Musk "Terafab" signal; AMD-vs-Nvidia debate | Barron's, Motley Fool | Sentiment wildcard for AMD vs. peers |
| Broad market | Q3 beats (Meta, Tesla, IBM, TI); indices up | Zacks, IBD, Stocktwits | Supportive risk-on backdrop |

- The forward figure is almost certainly a non-GAAP, consensus-style number, so the 35x forward P/E is not a like-for-like GAAP multiple. The tools give no analyst-estimate detail to verify it.
- The low PEG of 0.53 only holds if that forward growth is delivered.
- A beta of 2.45 means large drawdowns are possible on any growth disappointment.

## 2. Income Statement Trends

Q4 figures are not in the quarterly feed, because 10-Qs omit Q4. Gaps are noted below.

| Quarter ended | Revenue ($M) | Gross margin | Operating income ($M) | Op margin | Net income ($M) | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 2024 | 6,819 | 50.1% | 724 | 10.6% | 771 | 0.47 |

- **The supply risks aren't addressed.** CoWoS packaging limits, HBM allocation (Kindig says only about 15% is left beyond Nvidia, Alphabet and AMD), and a Morgan Stanley estimate cut are all flagged. Those directly threaten a ramp the forward EPS depends on.
- **Several headlines say outright that AMD is "priced for perfection."** When a stock is positioned that way, an in-line print can still fall.

- **The breakout failed.** You say the stock is "retesting" the September breakout. A retest holds above the broken level. AMD has closed back below the 6/30 high area (580.91 close, 584.73 high), which is a failed breakout until proven otherwise.
- **The decline had weight.** The three heaviest down days were 22.3M, 28.8M and 22.6M shares, including a **-5.4% gap-down on 10/15 with no earnings catalyst** (540.00 open versus 570.82 prior close).

  - MACD (-2.17) and the histogram (-13.29) haven't confirmed. Price is still under the 10 EMA (566), the VWMA (590) and the Bollinger midline (599).
- **"RSI never reached oversold" cuts both ways.** It means there was no washout or capitulation. And the RSI divergence at the 10/6 peak (72.16 versus 72.99 on 9/25) is a classic top signature.
- **The overhead supply is large.** Everyone who bought between about 580 and 650 is underwater, and the VWMA says much of the volume traded up there.
- **Next support is not close.** After 523 (the lower band) comes the 493–516 range, then the 200 SMA at 399, about 28% below.

## 7. Your macro story contradicts itself

You attribute the selloff to a market-wide wobble, citing "market has cracked" and "all hell breaking loose," and you also say the macro backdrop is benign. You can't have both. If the macro fear is real, a beta of 2.45 means AMD takes roughly 2.5 times the damage. If it isn't, the selloff was AMD-specific. Also, Polymarket's 8% recession probability and 97% no-cuts reading mean a stable backdrop is already priced. A surprise has only one direction to go. I don't have yield or VIX data (the FRED calls failed), so I'm not claiming rates are rising, only that nothing in the data shows relief.

## Bottom line

AMD is a good company at a price that assumes everything goes right. Earnings land on Nov 3, a date from a single X post, not confirmed by the data. The setup is:

- A forward EPS target about 2.9x the current run-rate
- A 1% FCF yield and no buyback support
- Falling sequential cash flow and an unexplained $307M non-operating contribution
- Only insider selling
- A technical structure that has broken below its breakout level on heavy volume
- A crowded long that is already labeled "priced for perfection"

The upside case needs a beat, a raise and a stable macro backdrop. The downside case needs only one of those to slip, and the last time this stock set a high it gave back 26% in a month.

**What would change my mind:** a print showing FCF recovering with capex stabilizing, a clean explanation of the non-operating gain, guidance that supports the $15.76 path, and a close back above 585 on rising volume. Until then, I'd rather wait for the earnings reaction than pay for perfection ahead of it.
